title: Widespread Bell outage affecting 911 and other calls in Newfoundland and Labrador
summary: The RCMP, Royal Newfoundland Constabulary, Newfoundland Power and City of St. John's are some organizations who say their phones lines are affected by the widespread Bell outage.

image.caption: The RCMP says the cause of the outage is unknown. (CBC)

blocks.text: The RCMP, Royal Newfoundland Constabulary, Newfoundland Power and City of St. John's are some organizations who say their phones lines are affected by the widespread Bell outage.
The cause of the outage is not known
A widespread Bell telecommunications outage is affecting calls in Newfoundland and Labrador, including some people trying to call 911 and other non-emergency police phone lines.
In a social media post, Bell Aliant said customers may not be able to make voice calls, including to emergency services.

"We are working to restore service as quickly as possible. If you require emergency assistance, please go directly to the nearest fire station, police station or hospital emergency department," reads the statement.
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary says its non-emergency telephone reporting line is unavailable, but says its 911 system isn't affected.
"Customer service and emergency phone lines are currently unavailable," reads a social media post from the utility.
Newfoundland Power says people can call 709-685-5078 for power outages, downed lines, or other electricity system emergencies only.
The City of St. John's says its 311 service is not available to Bell customers, either.
